metadata.note: Missouri Pacific in Kansas (and its Colorado main line to Pueblo), including the Central Branch Union Pacific. Research report: research/branches/missouri_pacific_in_kansas.txt (researched 2026-11-17). Every feature draws exactly its block's drawable: span; blocks whose drawable is NONE are omitted. Missouri Pacific features carry the company's existing colour, pulled programmatically from data/missouri_pacific_eagle.geojson (mp-missouri-river-eagle). The Central Branch Union Pacific's own operation (1868-1880, Atchison - Waterville) is a separate feature in a new colour on identical geometry to its Missouri Pacific 1881+ counterpart (Rule 4 split at the December 1880 lease). The Kansas City - Leavenworth - Atchison - Falls City features are the Kansas City - Omaha half of the Missouri River Eagle route and are separate from the existing mp-missouri-river-eagle feature (St. Louis - Kansas City), which is not modified. headway_min values are estimates throughout; avg_speed_kmh values are estimates except where speed_source names a schedule.

metadata.ownership_split: Central Branch Union Pacific -> Missouri Pacific at the December 1880 lease (WCB, LOK): cbup-atchison-waterville 1868-1880 and mp-ks-atchison-waterville 1881-1951 share identical geometry. No CBUP-era passenger year is confirmed west of Waterville, so the Waterville - Downs and Yuma - Warwick lines are Missouri Pacific only. Gould control from Jan 1880, the 1893-98 receivership, the 1898/1899 reorganisations and the 1909 merger are not treated as operator changes. Every other Kansas line was built by a paper subsidiary (CGO&O, K&C, K&CP, DM&A, W&C, SLFS&W, FSW&W, L&CVAL, Nevada & Minden, Rooks County, KH&P ...) and drawn as Missouri Pacific from opening; no evidence any ran trains in its own name.

CENTRAL BRANCH 1893-1898: whether the UP receivership operated the line apart from MP (a temporary operator split) - not found. Whether the CBUP ran passenger trains west of Waterville 1877-1880 - not confirmed.

Start 1888: first Guide letters on the new line are 1887G (Quenemo, Gleason, Frederic, Giles City) and 1888G west of Hoisington and in Colorado (Holbrook, Arden, Boonville), so through Kansas City - Pueblo service is confirmed by 1888. Paola - Osawatomie is drawn with this feature per the report (same span). Trains: Scenic Limited (St. Louis - Pueblo - Denver/Salt Lake via D&RGW) before 1942; Colorado Eagle 21 June 1942 - March 1964 (WCE; SS57 16 June 1957 timetable confirms the route; OG52 Table 5 Oct 1 1951 times Council Grove 11:48, Herington 12:14, Lindsborg 12:52, Hoisington 1:15); unnamed successor trains after the name was dropped. A Kansas City - Hoisington coach also ran (OG52 Nos. 15/16). End 1966: Schafer (via WCE): 'On April 2, 1966, the MP canceled the remaining unnamed trains serving Denver, ending passenger service along the Colorado Eagle's route west of Kansas City.' SOURCE CONFLICT, recorded not resolved: Fowler's Colorado file header says 'MP passenger service withdrawn 1964', yet the same file tags Eads, Sugar City, Ordway and Pueblo with his 1965t timetable letter - his 1964 is most likely the Colorado Eagle name-drop. 1966 (Schafer) is drawn; 1965 is the last year Fowler independently confirms; 1964 is Fowler's header. Pueblo - Denver was D&RGW track and is not drawn here. Santa Fe trains diverted onto MP between NA Junction and Avondale CO in 1968 (FCO) were Santa Fe service and do not extend this feature.
